Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: A notice has been posted about an optional training session happening next week.
Story: It was 2 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. On the other end, my friend’s voice trembled, barely holding together as they told me about the terrible news that had just shattered their family. I sat up, heart pounding, listening as they sobbed, desperate for comfort. I knew what they needed—someone to just be there, to listen, to help them feel less alone in the darkness. But as I tried to focus on their words, my mind kept drifting to the notice I’d seen at work earlier that day: an optional training session next week, the kind that could make a difference in how the foreman saw me, maybe even lead to more hours or a better position. I was expected to be a reliable teammate, to show initiative, to prove I was serious about the job. But right now, my friend needed me, and I could hear the expectation in every shaky breath. I felt torn, the weight of both worlds pressing down on me, unsure which demand I could afford to let down.
